s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive facial swelling and orbital displacement
salient_findings: Painless, bony-hard swelling of the left cheek
Numbness of the left cheek and weakness in movement of the left upper lip
Expansion of the left maxillary ridge with mobility of primary teeth
Large, well-circumscribed, expansile, heterogeneous mass in the left maxillary sinus
key_facts: 9-year-old boy with left cheek swelling and hyperglobus of the left eye
Hyperglobus first noted 1 year earlier
Swelling of the left cheek developed 6 months later
Marked progression of swelling over the preceding 3 months
Normal overlying skin
Numbness of the left cheek and weakness in movement of the left upper lip
No other neurologic deficits, no visual disturbances, and ocular motility intact
Expansion of the left maxillary ridge with mobility of primary teeth c, d, and e
Large, well-circumscribed, expansile, heterogeneous mass in the left maxillary sinus
Deviation and destruction of the nasal septum
Invasion of the ethmoid sinus
Thinning, displacement, and perforation of the anterior wall of the sphenoid sinus
Destruction of the pterygoid plates
Elevation and perforation of the left infraorbital rim
Extreme postero-superior displacement of the second molar toward the inferior orbital fissure

shortlist.label: Cherubism
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by bilateral expansion of the jawbones, but can present unilaterally, with a heterogeneous mass in the maxillary sinus and orbital displacement

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause expansile, heterogeneous lesions in the maxillary sinus and lead to facial asymmetry and orbital displacement

shortlist.label: Central giant cell granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Typically presents as a well-circumscribed, expansile lesion in the jaw, which can cause facial swelling and orbital displacement

shortlist.label: Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Although rare, can present with nasal obstruction and facial swelling, and may extend into the maxillary sinus and orbit

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: A rare, aggressive tumor that can present with a rapidly expanding mass in the maxillary sinus, causing facial swelling and orbital displacement

raw.rationale: The patient's age, sex, and clinical presentation of bilateral cheek swelling and hyperglobus, along with the radiographic findings of a well-circumscribed, expansile, heterogeneous mass in the maxillary sinus, are consistent with Cherubism. The disease typically presents in childhood, often with a family history, and can cause expansion of the jaw and orbital displacement.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: While fibrous dysplasia can cause jaw expansion and orbital displacement, it typically presents with a ground-glass appearance on radiographs, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Central giant cell granuloma
rejected.why: This lesion can cause jaw expansion, but it is often more aggressive and can have a more variable radiographic appearance than described in this case.

rejected.label: Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma
rejected.why: This tumor typically presents with nasal obstruction and epistaxis, which are not described in this case, and is more common in adolescent males.

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: This malignant tumor can cause jaw destruction and orbital displacement, but it typically presents with more systemic symptoms, such as fever and weight loss, and has a more aggressive radiographic appearance than described in this case.
